html:
Ajina Tepa is the ruin of a Buddhist monastery in the Vakhsh valley of southern Tajikistan, built in the 7th and 8th centuries, in the last years before Islam came to the region.

Its name means hill of the demons. When Soviet archaeologists dug it in the 1960s they found a monastery court and a stupa court, with painted clay sculpture, and a reclining Buddha in his final rest, about 13 metres long. Cut into pieces and moved to Dushanbe, it is now the largest Buddha figure in Central Asia, shown in the national museum.

Ajina Tepa shows how far Buddhism had spread along the Oxus, in the old lands of Bactria and the Kushans, before the Arab conquest.
sum: Ajina Tepa is the ruin of a Buddhist monastery in the Vakhsh valley of southern Tajikistan, built in the 7th and 8th centuries, in the last years before Islam came to the region.
